headline: You can pay for this in phases between November 2026 and 2029. Judge each lot by its all-in cost (land plus water, septic, power and grading), because County permit fees are small next to the cost of site work.
key_points: Here is the phased timeline. Nov-Dec 2026: research and site visits. Jan-Feb 2027: make an offer with a 45-60 day due-diligence period. Mar 2027: close. Late Mar-Apr 2027: a 2-3 week Bhutan trip while the designer starts. Apr-Aug 2027: survey, percolation (perc) test, biology survey, design and engineering, then submit plans. Sep-Dec 2027: plan check and permits, then move the trailer on, grade, and put in septic, water and power. 2028: build. Late 2028-2029: final inspection. From 2029: pods, orchard and a longer Bhutan stay.

5-acre lots start around $25k, but judge each one by its all-in cost: land plus water, septic, power, grading and driveway. Asking prices in 2026 run about $25k-$60k for remote dirt-road lots and $60k-$180k near Yucca Valley with utilities close by. Pioneertown and Pipes Canyon run $225k-$475k. Site work can cost more than the house: septic $12k-$60k and power $15k-$80k (estimates).

Where a water main is close, district water costs a fixed fee. Hi-Desert Water District (HDWD) charges $5,418 for a 5/8-inch sprinkler-ready service or $10,836 for a 1-inch service. On top of that come a $200 fire-flow fee and installation at cost ($600 minimum). A main extension is billed at actual cost. Bighorn-Desert View Water Agency (BDVWA) lists $16,201 plus a $3,040 installation fee. Joshua Basin's fees differ, so get a written quote. A private well runs roughly $25k-$100k+ (estimate). A permitted house can't rely on hauled water.

County permit fees are modest. In fiscal year 2026-27, combined plan check and inspection for a small wood-frame custom house is about $2,428, or about $3,540-$3,700 if the house is classed 'hillside' (ask County Building and Safety whether a house under 1,000 sq ft pays the full base fee). Plans go in after July 1, 2027, so budget at the rates already set for that date. Land Use Services (LUS) charges $310 for the temporary trailer permit, $268 for the RV site (ask whether both apply) and $264 for each yearly renewal. Grading under 100 cubic yards is free; 100-1,000 cubic yards costs $713-$798. A cargo container costs $160 plus $200 for plan review.

Small pods keep fees low. Accessory dwelling units (ADUs) of 500 sq ft or less avoid impact fees, and ADUs under 500 sq ft avoid school fees. The main house will likely owe school fees on all of its living area. The 2026 state cap is $5.38 per sq ft, so a 500 sq ft house owes at most about $2,690 (ask Morongo Unified School District for its rate).

Joshua tree fees drop to zero if every pad, septic field, trench, fence and driveway stays more than 50 ft from every western Joshua tree, including trees on neighboring lots. If that isn't possible, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) charges in-lieu fees for every stem. The whole Morongo Basin is in the standard fee area, where 2026 fees are $354.75 (under 1 m), $521.75 (1-5 m) or $2,609 (5 m+) per stem. CDFW has no deadline to act on a permit, so a permit can stall the schedule. CDFW must re-set its fees by June 30, 2027.

The California FAIR Plan (Fair Access to Insurance Requirements, the state's insurer of last resort) covers the house against named perils only, such as fire, lightning and smoke. It never covers theft or liability. Optional vandalism cover stops once the dwelling has been vacant or unoccupied for more than 30 days in a row. A house under construction without furniture counts as vacant. Rates rise an average 29.1% for new and renewing policies from Oct 15, 2026.

Earning all 12 FAIR Plan hardening discounts cuts the wildfire part of the premium by up to 16.4%. Design for them from the start: a Class A roof, enclosed eaves, ember-resistant vents, multi-pane windows, 6 in. of noncombustible material at the base of the walls, a 5 ft noncombustible zone around the house, and pods, containers and sheds placed more than 30 ft from the house.

You can pay cash in phases: land, then studies and permits, then water, septic and power, then the shell, then the finishes. Refinance after the certificate of occupancy. Land loans and owner-builder construction loans are scarce (ask two local lenders or a credit union). If the seller finances, close through escrow with a recorded deed of trust and an owner's title policy. Price solar at full cost: the federal 30% Residential Clean Energy Credit ended for systems placed in service after Dec 31, 2025.

Budget tiers, including land and a 15-25% cushion (estimates): lean do-it-yourself (DIY) at about 400 sq ft, $217k-$479k; balanced at about 500 sq ft, $432k-$874k; mostly hired at about 600 sq ft, $766k-$1.6M. A whole-floor hydronic radiant system costs about $15k-$35k. A cork, wool or floor-heating tatami finish adds $2k-$20k (estimates). If the lot is inside Town limits, the Town's 725 sq ft minimum raises the cost (ask Town Planning).

Once the house permit is issued, you can live on the lot in a used, Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)-registered travel trailer ($8k-$25k, estimate). The imported capsule costs more than its price tag. A $19k-$24k listing becomes at least $25k-$37k after 28-53% import duties. Placed on the lot with freight, crane, foundation and hookups, it likely costs $35k-$65k (estimates). An uncertified capsule never qualifies as the temporary home.

The first Bhutan trip fits in late Mar-Apr 2027, right after closing, while the designer starts. Keep belongings in a storage unit in town, since the lot has no permits yet. Two weeks for two costs about $8,400-$12,600 on the ground, or $11,000-$18,000 with flights (estimates). The $100-a-night Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) is guaranteed only to Aug 31, 2027. Save the longer stay for 2029. A mid-build trip works only right after a passed inspection, for under about 5 months. Get any extension approved in writing before you leave. Carrying costs while you build run about $5k-$10k a year (property tax, insurance, fixed utility charges, permit renewals, storage), plus a caretaker while you're away.

risks.risk: Water, septic, power, grading and driveway costs exceed the cost of the house, for example a private well or a long Southern California Edison (SCE) line extension.
risks.mitigation: Get written quotes from the water district, SCE and a septic designer during the 45-60 day due-diligence period. Prefer lots with a water main and power at the lot line. Carry a 15-25% cushion.

risks.risk: Belongings left on the lot are stolen or damaged by heat while you're abroad, and no insurance pays: the FAIR Plan has no theft cover, and its vandalism cover ends after 30 days vacant.
risks.mitigation: For the 2027 trip, use a storage unit in town that has its own contents policy. Later, use a permitted storage container (a County accessory-structure permit, plus a Temporary Use Permit and a removal bond if no house exists yet), a cellular camera and a caretaker. Buy a separate policy that covers the absence (ask an insurance broker).

risks.risk: The building permit or temporary trailer permit lapses during a long trip, which brings new fees and can force you out of the trailer.
risks.mitigation: Take the first trip in late Mar-Apr 2027, before any permit exists, and save the long stay for 2029. Mid-build, pass an inspection right before leaving and stay away under about 5 months. Get any extension approved in writing first (ask County Building and Safety).

risks.risk: Joshua trees near building areas bring per-stem fees and a CDFW review with no deadline.
risks.mitigation: Have a biologist count stems before removing contingencies. Make the purchase contingent on finding a building area more than 50 ft from every tree, including trees on neighboring lots.

risks.risk: The imported capsule costs far more than $20k once placed and can't be registered or permitted as a home.
risks.mitigation: Before paying, get certification papers and a delivered, duty-paid quote, or buy a used, DMV-registered US travel trailer instead.

risks.risk: A helper gets hurt on site. If you pay helpers you may be their employer and responsible for workers' compensation. Anyone hired for a job over $1,000 must hold a state contractor's license.
risks.mitigation: For paid work, hire licensed contractors who carry workers' compensation. Read the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) owner-builder guide, and ask an insurance broker about owner-builder liability cover.

questions_for_couple: What is the most we will spend in total, and at what amount do we stop and re-plan?
Where do we live from closing in Mar 2027 until the house permit is issued (likely Sep-Dec 2027): a rental nearby, an RV park, or somewhere else?
Which tier fits us: lean DIY at about 400 sq ft, balanced at about 500, or mostly hired at about 600? How much of the work does each of us want to do?
Do we prefer a cheaper remote lot with more DIY infrastructure, or a pricier lot with water and power at the lot line?
Do we live in a used travel trailer first and add a capsule later as a permitted unit, or skip the capsule?
What is our progress pledge (for example, a passed inspection every 2-3 months, and never more than 5), and what spending amount needs both of us to agree?
How much of the travel budget goes to the 2027 Bhutan trip, and how much do we save for a longer stay in 2029?
next_actions: Look up the lot's Assessor's Parcel Number (APN) on the County assessor map viewer (assessormapviewer.arc.sbcounty.gov). Note its recorded acreage (5.00 or more?), its Tax Rate Area, and whether it is inside Town of Yucca Valley limits. @computer
Walk the lot on your next visit. Photograph the tag number on the nearest power pole, note the nearest fire hydrant or water meter, and roughly count Joshua tree stems near likely pads. @land

Call the lot's water district (Hi-Desert Water District 760-365-8333, Bighorn-Desert View Water Agency 760-364-2315, or Joshua Basin Water District 760-366-8438). Ask how far away the nearest main is, and ask for a written all-in quote for a 1-inch service and a will-serve letter. @phone

Call County Building and Safety (909-387-8311), or Town Planning (760-369-6575) if the lot is in Town. Ask whether a house under 1,000 sq ft pays the full base fee, whether the lot falls in the 'hillside' fee category, and which fee rates apply to plans submitted in Aug 2027. @phone
Call Southern California Edison (SCE) with the pole tag number. Ask for a ballpark cost and lead time to bring power to the lot. @phone

Email the capsule seller. Ask for California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD), U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or Recreational Vehicle Industry Association (RVIA) certification papers. Ask whether the unit has a vehicle identification number (VIN) that the California DMV can register, and ask for a delivered, duty-paid price to ZIP 92284. @email

Call three insurance brokers who place California FAIR Plan policies (find them through cfpnet.com). Ask for written quotes on vacant-land liability, a dwelling under construction, an RV policy for the trailer, and stored contents during a 3-week absence and a 5-month absence. @phone
Email the business office of Morongo Unified School District. Ask its residential fee per sq ft, and whether a new house or an ADU under 500 sq ft owes it. @email

Build a budget spreadsheet with the three tiers. Enter your real cash on hand, a 15-25% cushion, $5k-$10k a year in carrying costs and the County fees that take effect July 1, 2027. Add calendar reminders for July 1, 2027 (County fees rise) and Aug 31, 2027 (Bhutan's $100 SDF guarantee ends). @computer
Sit down with the spreadsheet and agree on a total ceiling, a stop-and-review amount, and the spending amount that needs both of you to approve. @together
